title: AD16 Modulates Microglial Activation and Polarization to Mitigate Neuroinflammation in Ischemic Stroke Models Through alpha7nAChR-ERK-STAT3 Signaling.
authors: Zhao, Guo-Jian; Zhang, Li-Mei; Wang, Si-Rou; Yang, Mei; Jiang, Jia-Hao; Yuan, Bo-Xiang; Huang, Cheng; Huang, Zhi-Hua; Tang, Xiao-Lu; Chen, Tao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究AD16化合物通过alpha7nAChR-ERK-STAT3通路调节小胶质细胞极化减轻脑缺血神经炎症，仅涉及分子对接作为辅助手段，核心为湿实验药理学研究，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA结合建模无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation constitutes a critical pathological event subsequent to ischemic stroke. AD16, a novel anti-neuroinflammatory compound, has demonstrated efficacy in alleviating neuroinflammation in neonatal rats induced by ischemia-hypoxia. This study aims to elucidate the therapeutic utility and underlying mechanisms of AD16 in an adult ischemic stroke rat model. METHODS: A rat transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model was employed. Neurological function was evaluated using the Longa and Garcia JH scores, motor function was assessed through rotary rod and CatWalk gait analysis, and brain injury was examined via TTC and Nissl staining. Molecular docking techniques simulate the binding of a target compound to a potential target. Western blot, immunofluorescence, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were used to detect microglia phenotype, pro-inflammatory factors, and activation of signaling molecules. RESULTS: AD16 treatment improved neural function in tMCAO rats, reduced cerebral infarction volume and brain water content, preserved blood-brain barrier integrity, and inhibited pro-inflammatory cytokines. Molecular docking showed AD16 has high affinity for alpha7nAChR, TLR4, ERK, and STAT3. AD16 increased alpha7nAChR, CD206, and p-ERK protein levels, while decreasing CD40, CD68, TLR4, and p-STAT3. These effects were reversed by alpha-BTX (alpha7nAChR inhibitor) and U0126 (ERK inhibitor). CONCLUSION: AD16 may inhibit microglia activation and polarization via the alpha7nAChR-ERK-STAT3 pathway, thus reducing neuroinflammation from cerebral ischemia and protecting the brain. This study suggests AD16 as a potential treatment for ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 背景：神经炎症（neuroinflammation）是缺血性卒中后的关键病理事件。AD16作为一种新型抗神经炎症化合物，已在缺血缺氧诱导的新生大鼠中显示出缓解神经炎症的功效。本研究旨在阐明AD16在成年缺血性卒中大鼠模型中的治疗效用及潜在机制。方法：采用大鼠短暂大脑中动脉闭塞（tMCAO）模型。通过Longa和Garcia JH评分评估神经功能，通过旋转杆和CatWalk步态分析评估运动功能，并通过TTC和尼氏染色检查脑损伤。分子对接技术模拟目标化合物与潜在靶点的结合。使用Western blot、免疫荧光和酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）检测小胶质细胞表型、促炎因子及信号分子的激活。结果：AD16治疗改善了tMCAO大鼠的神经功能，减少了脑梗死体积和脑含水量，保持了血脑屏障完整性，并抑制了促炎细胞因子。分子对接显示AD16对alpha7nAChR、TLR4、ERK和STAT3具有高亲和力。AD16增加了alpha7nAChR、CD206和p-ERK蛋白水平，同时降低了CD40、CD68、TLR4和p-STAT3。这些效应被alpha-BTX（alpha7nAChR抑制剂）和U0126（ERK抑制剂）逆转。结论：AD16可能通过alpha7nAChR-ERK-STAT3通路抑制小胶质细胞激活和极化，从而减轻脑缺血引起的神经炎症并保护大脑。本研究提示AD16可作为缺血性卒中的潜在治疗药物。
